geology_notes: The Hells Gate Antimony Project sits in Central Newfoundland on the Exploits Subzone, a well-documented geological corridor for orogenic antimony deposits. The NI 43-101 technical report on file is dated August 2023 and yielded no extractable resource or reserve table rows — the project remains at the geological assessment and drill-target stage with no compliant mineral resource estimate. The May 2026 correction release materially revised the previously reported Frost Cove intervals down to two validated intersections: FC25-17 (2.00% Sb / 0.10m) and FC25-27 (13.00% Sb / 0.57m). Nine additional 2026 drill holes from the northern Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond program remain pending assay as of this run; those results, once published, are the single most important geological disclosure on the horizon. The June 15 scorecard noted a second new polymetallic system discovery at the southern Frost Cove shaft (7.25% Sb / 1.98m), which expanded the conceptual footprint but has not been independently verified within this run's fetch limit. Score stays at 2 until a maiden inferred resource is established under NI 43-101.

A strategically priced financing at a premium to market, or an institutional placement, would begin to justify the structure; without it, the per-share NAV hurdle remains a persistent drag.
catalyst_notes: The antimony macro context remains the dominant factor: China's September 2024 export controls on antimony have driven spot prices to multi-decade highs and elevated the strategic priority of western-jurisdiction supply. Newfoundland and Labrador has an active critical minerals strategy and good access infrastructure for exploration-stage companies. These structural tailwinds benefit any western antimony asset regardless of company-specific execution. On the company-specific side, the nine pending 2026 Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond drill assays are the primary near-term binary catalyst — positive results with improved widths and grades (relative to the corrected May 2026 baseline) would be a meaningful re-rating event. No company-specific catalysts (resource update, strategic partnership, government grant, offtake LOI) were confirmed in today's search. Score of 3 reflects macro support plus the pending drill results as a near-term catalyst, offset by the absence of confirmed company-specific news.
acquisition_notes: Without a compliant NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate, a P/NAV multiple cannot be calculated and peer-comparable acquisition analysis is not possible. The strategic case for Hells Gate is real — a western-hemisphere antimony asset in a stable mining jurisdiction is exactly what defence-supply-chain buyers, battery manufacturers, and major producers are seeking given China-supply risk. However, any acquisition premium at this stage would be priced on exploration blue-sky, not defined resource value, which limits the achievable multiple. The Golden Baie and Black Raven additions broaden the district footprint but do not change the absence of a resource anchor. Score advances when a resource estimate provides a NAV anchor against which acquisition comparables ($/t Sb, EV/resource oz equivalent) can be applied.
analyst_summary: Churchill Resources (CRI.V) holds the Hells Gate Antimony Project in Central Newfoundland — a western-hemisphere antimony asset in the right commodity and the right jurisdiction, but still at the exploration stage with no compliant NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate. China's 2024 export controls have made antimony a genuinely critical-mineral story: spot prices are elevated, western governments are funding supply-chain alternatives, and Newfoundland has the infrastructure and regulatory framework to advance projects efficiently. That macro tailwind is real and keeps Hells Gate on the radar of acquirers and strategics. The constraints are structural. At 316.7M shares outstanding, no defined resource, and no confirmed company-specific catalysts in today's news scan, the per-share upside path remains unquantifiable. The May 2026 data-correction release revised Frost Cove intervals downward — a credibility event that has not been offset by new disclosure. Nine 2026 drill holes from the northern Frost Cove / Pomley Cove Pond program remain pending assay; those results are the single most important near-term disclosure. Confidence is LOW because the analytical gap — no resource estimate, no accessible IR page, no management disclosure or insider ownership data — is too wide to support a high-conviction call. Inflection points that would drive a BUY consideration: (1) maiden inferred resource published under NI 43-101, (2) drill assays from the nine pending 2026 holes showing improved widths and grades, (3) strategic partnership or government funding announcement. Until one of those occurs, WATCH and do not size.
